premise.claim: When a pod has a nodeAffinity with no required terms (e.g. only a preferred term on another label), hasRepeatedLocality returns false before checking spec.nodeSelector, so NodeAffinityWithCache injects the tiered locality affinity on top of the pod's own locality nodeSelector; with the required policy that yields two contradicting requirements (rack-b from nodeSelector, rack-a injected) and the pod stays Pending. (issue #6280)
premise.evidence: On base 253f6bb the contract tests FAIL (pod gets RequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution {topology.kubernetes.io/rack In [rack-a]} injected on top of nodeSelector {rack: rack-b}); on head e6d2213 they PASS. See results/base-reviewer-harness.txt, results/base-new-tests.txt, results/head-reviewer-harness.txt.

findings.claim: hasRepeatedLocality must fall through to the spec.nodeSelector check when the pod's nodeAffinity has no required terms (preferred-only or empty).

Mutate must not inject a required locality affinity (and must keep the pod's own affinity/nodeSelector untouched) when the pod already pins a tiered locality label via spec.nodeSelector, even if the pod has a preferred-only node affinity.

liveNote: L3 intentionally skipped for this review (debate pipeline runs unit + integration only). The change is a pure admission-time decision in one webhook plugin; the fake-client Mutate tests cover the injected-pod shape. A live check, if ever needed: create a Dataset+AlluxioRuntime with cache affinity rack=rack-a, then a pod labeled fluid.io/dataset.<name>.sched=required with nodeSelector {topology.kubernetes.io/rack: rack-b} and a preferred affinity on another label; the mutated pod must have no requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution injected.
